title: carbon.teaching.v1
description: One JSON file per record, under an agent's own store at teachings/<id>.json. What a client taught their agent, or what the agent refused as a change for the people who build it. A declared field of the wrong type is refused; a field this version does not name is carried, so a record an older or a newer writer wrote is never parked on a strict key check. There is no maxLength here because carbon's validator implements none: the length cap is the declaration's teaching.max_chars and the writer enforces it, naming the cap in its refusal.

id.description: teach-<utc compact>-<first 8 of the sha256 of source_message_id>.

kind.description: An instruction the agent remembered, or an instruction it refused and raised as a change for the people who build it. One shape, two kinds: there is no second schema for a change request.

agent.description: The agent id, as in the declaration.

text.description: For an instruction, what the agent will now do, in plain words. For a change request, what the client asked for. At most the declaration's teaching.max_chars.

conversation_id.description: Channel-native, as in the message record.

source_message_id.description: The <conversation_id>:<platform message id> of the inbound capture that taught it. A record whose source is not a capture in this agent's own store is refused before any write.

taught_by.description: Copied from the cited capture and never supplied by the caller, so an instruction cannot be attributed to someone who did not send it. sender_name is absent when the capture carries none.

release_id.description: The release the turn that wrote this record was taking, when a runtime named one. It is written by the teaching server from what the release loop told it and never by the model, and it is absent when the server was started by something that runs no release loop, such as a scored run. It is what lets the runtime ask, at the end of a turn in the management conversation, whether anything was recorded in that turn.

status.description: active or forgotten for an instruction; open or closed for a change request. A revocation is a status change and never a delete: there is no path here that takes a record away.

failed_question.description: Change requests only: which boundary question was answered yes. 1 a tool the agent does not have, 2 a system, channel or person it does not reach, 3 a permission it was not given, 4 a change to what was agreed to be done for this client; size is the instruction that does not fit under the caps.

forgotten.description: Written when the client revoked the instruction, absent otherwise. The revoking message is named so the revocation is as traceable as the instruction was.

reviewed.description: Written when someone at PcL read this record from the studio and marked it read, absent otherwise. It is a marker and nothing else: it changes no status, revokes no instruction and closes no change request. It exists because carbon teachings prints a standing list and a person sitting down to it weekly could not tell a record taught yesterday from one they read three weeks ago, which is the whole value of reading the list.

closed.description: Written when a change request was closed from outside the box, absent otherwise. The work item's id is the one field of it that ever reaches the box: nothing here mints, reads or closes one.
